paper_metadata.title: Eye closure sensitivity in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy and its effect on prognosis

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study used a consecutive sample of patients diagnosed by standard ILAE criteria. The setting and recruitment period are clear, and baseline characteristics are well-described, minimizing selection bias.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: We included 76 consecutive patients diagnosed with JME according to the ILAE criteria who had at least one year of follow-up
items.reasoning: The authors specify the diagnostic criteria and the consecutive nature of the sample from a specialized neurology department.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: We included 76 consecutive patients diagnosed with JME according to the ILAE criteria
items.reasoning: Consecutive recruitment in a clinical setting is a standard method to reduce selection bias.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: JME was diagnosed as a specific electroclinical syndrome with bilateral, single or repetitive, arrhythmic, irregular myoclonic jerks predominantly in the arms starting at puberty... The EEG should show rapid generalized and often irregular spike waves
items.reasoning: The study uses standard ILAE diagnostic criteria and specifies a minimum follow-up of one year.

items.evidence_snippet: We included 76 consecutive patients
items.reasoning: The use of consecutive patients suggests that all eligible individuals seen at the clinic during the study period were included.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The data on gender, age at onset of epilepsy, seizure types, febrile seizures, consanguinity, family history of epilepsy, response to anti-epileptic drugs (AEDs), comorbid conditions, MRI findings, and follow-up duration were retrospectively recorded
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides a comprehensive breakdown of these characteristics across the three prognostic groups.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (ECS) is clearly defined and measured using standardized EEG protocols. The retrospective re-evaluation by two investigators with consensus reaching helps ensure reliability.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Generalized spike- or multispike-wave discharges in the resting EEG that appeared on at least two occasions after eye closure (excluding the IPS period) were accepted as ECS.
items.reasoning: The authors provide a specific, operationalized definition of Eye Closure Sensitivity.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: All of the available EEG traces were re-evaluated retrospectively by two investigators, and consensus was reached in a joint session when needed.
items.reasoning: The use of two expert reviewers and a consensus process increases the reliability of the EEG interpretation.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: appeared on at least two occasions after eye closure
items.reasoning: The cut-point for ECS is based on established clinical descriptions rather than being derived from the study's own data distribution.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: For the EEG recordings, the electrodes were placed according to the international 10–20 system... The patients were instructed to close and open their eyes at least seven times during each EEG recording.
items.reasoning: A standardized EEG protocol was applied to all participants.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: detailed EEG records available for the re-evaluation of ECS... a total of 254 EEGs were re-analyzed
items.reasoning: The study only included patients with available EEG data, ensuring 100% completion for the analyzed sample.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: Imputation was not required as only patients with complete EEG records were included.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (prognosis/drug resistance) is defined using clear clinical thresholds for seizure frequency and medication adherence, which are standard in epilepsy research.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Patients experiencing more than one GTCS per year and/or more than five myoclonic or absence seizures/clusters per month despite the regular use of appropriately high doses of syndrome-specific AEDs were classified as the 'poor prognosis' group
items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly operationalized with specific seizure frequency thresholds.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The data on... response to anti-epileptic drugs (AEDs)... were retrospectively recorded in a standardized form.
items.reasoning: While the criteria are objective, the data relies on retrospective clinical records which may be subject to recall bias or inconsistent documentation.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The prognosis was evaluated only if the duration of effective therapy lasted more than 12 months.
items.reasoning: The same clinical criteria and minimum follow-up duration were applied to all patients.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Outcome of interest is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study identifies several confounders (family history, focal EEG findings) but does not use multivariable analysis to adjust for them when assessing the independent effect of ECS on prognosis.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: The data on gender, age at onset of epilepsy, seizure types, febrile seizures, consanguinity, family history of epilepsy, response to anti-epileptic drugs (AEDs), comorbid conditions, MRI findings
items.reasoning: The authors measured a wide range of clinical and demographic variables known to influence epilepsy prognosis.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: Focal spikes/sharp waves or recurrent 2- to 7-Hz localized slow wave paroxysms were interpreted as a focal abnormality.
items.reasoning: Confounders like focal abnormalities and pseudo-resistance are explicitly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: retrospectively recorded in a standardized form
items.reasoning: Reliability is limited by the retrospective nature of the data collection for clinical history (e.g., family history).

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The data... were retrospectively recorded in a standardized form.
items.reasoning: A standardized form was used for all participants.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).

items.reasoning: The study did not use matching or stratification in the design to control for confounders.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: The Chi-square test was used to compare the differences in the categorical variables between the groups.
items.reasoning: The analysis relied on univariable tests (Chi-square/Fisher exact). No multivariable regression was performed to adjust for confounders like family history or focal EEG findings.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Confounding Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Important potential confounders are appropriately accounted for, limiting potential bias with respect to the relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical analysis is limited to univariable comparisons. While appropriate for the small sample size, it limits the ability to determine the independent prognostic value of ECS. Reporting is transparent regarding the findings.

items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: The Chi-square test was used to compare the differences in the categorical variables between the groups. The SPSS 17.0 statistical software was used

items.evidence_snippet: Table 1 shows the clinical and EEG findings in the study groups.
